summary: The association review workbench. The reviewer is the association operator (with the superadmin), scoped to the association environment; no second role with the same access was added (DEC-0193). /assoc/vet-review lists every student, council-code and licence case in one server-paginated queue with filters for case type, status group, claim state (mine, unclaimed, others) and a name or code search, oldest waiting case first, linking to each case's review page; the trusted-veterinarian type joins through REVIEW_CASE_TYPES when PROMPT-010 creates it. A reviewer claims a submitted case, which moves it to UNDER_REVIEW with the claimer and time under an optimistic version check, so of two simultaneous claims exactly one succeeds; the holder releases it, and the superadmin may release someone else's claim only with a reason. A database CHECK ties a claim to UNDER_REVIEW, and the migration returns any unheld UNDER_REVIEW case of the workbench to the queue. Only the holder records structured checks from a closed per-type list (PASS, FAIL with a mandatory note, NOT_APPLICABLE), bound to the current submission version in an append-only table. All three decision functions now refuse a case held by another reviewer, refuse an approval while the latest result of any check on the current version is FAIL, and clear the claim; an unclaimed submitted case can still be decided in one step, and the mandatory reason and version lock were already in place. A corrected resubmission starts unchecked. Claim, release, checks and decisions are audited with actor, context, case, old and new status, time and reason; every view of a private professional document now also records the case, submission version, document kind and case status at that moment; audit_event is append-only in the database (a trigger refuses UPDATE and DELETE except the actor foreign key's own ON DELETE SET NULL). Documents of the current version are previewed inline in a lazily loaded frame that loads only when opened; the file route now sends X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN, frame-ancestors 'self', and for images a sandbox with default-src 'none'. The payment boundary is enforced at the tag service: the LICENSED and TRUSTED tags are accepted only from the server (null actor), so association operators, reviewers and the superadmin get FORBIDDEN; licence approval reaches only LICENSE_APPROVED_AWAITING_PAYMENT, no reviewer move reaches ACTIVE_LICENSED_VET, billing has no manual paid function and membership activation refuses an unpaid account. The UI is Persian RTL with labelled filters, a search landmark, status roles and a navigation entry, and fits a phone.

limitations: The reviewer role is the existing association operator; there is no separate reviewer role, so every association operator can review every professional case.

Claiming is optional: an unclaimed submitted case can still be decided in one step, protected by the version lock. A claim has no automatic expiry; a stale claim is released by its holder or by the superadmin with a reason.
Trusted-veterinarian review is not in the workbench yet; its case type and checks arrive with PROMPT-010/011.
Checks are advisory except FAIL, which blocks approval; approval does not require every check to be recorded.
PDF previews are not sandboxed because a sandbox disables the browser's PDF viewer; they are protected by same-origin framing, nosniff and the byte-signature check at upload.
The audit_event trigger makes the trail append-only for every writer, including future maintenance scripts.
Pagination beyond one page is covered by the shared query contract but not exercised in the browser.
The full browser matrix was not rerun; ten suites through the changed code were.
Screenshots were not captured; visual fidelity of the new page is unverified.
